description: Fires most strongly when column 1 (second from left) is tall and topped by at least two of the side-to-move's stones, with column 0 empty or nearly so; stronger the taller the stack, weaker as stones (especially opponent's) fill columns 0 and 2 and as the game gets longer, boosted when the opponent's last move was in columns 4-6. A weaker early-game route: opponent just stacked on my single column-1 stone. Covers only a minority of firing.
effect: None measurable: forcing it to zero or to its max changes no column's probability by more than about 2 points (4 positions tested).
notes: Layer 1. Best dev F1 0.236 (P 0.31, R 0.19, AUROC 0.59), sim share 0.05 (p5). The column-1 stack with column 0 empty is a real driver in minimal pairs: flipping ownership kills it, the mirrored column 5 does not work, column 0 stones hurt, and the activation reaches 4.16 in synthesis. But act tests show strong context dependence (ply, other columns, last move column multiplies it), and most firing positions (bands 5-7) follow no rule I found. Tried: top-mine only (F1 0.08), neighbour exposure (0.12), col0-empty stack (0.17), with opponent-col-2 filter (0.18, P 0.48), loosened (0.19). Looks like a mixture or distributed direction.
